nodes.description: Two damaged copies of NDUFB8, in a compound-heterozygous configuration in both 2018 patients. Patient 1 carried p.Pro76Gln in trans with p.Cys144Trp; Pro76 lies in a highly conserved matrix-side region above the ND5 lateral helix and close to ND4, while Cys144 sits in the membrane domain and appears to form a disulfide with Cys279 of ND5. Patient 2 carried p.Tyr62His, at a residue whose hydroxyl hydrogen-bonds to Asp74 of NDUFB8 and which lies 4 to 5 angstrom from Pro76 in the same conserved patch, in trans with the frameshift p.Glu63Aspfs*35 (c.189delA). ClinGen's 2024 recuration counted five unique variants across the three published cases and read the mechanism as loss of function.

nodes.description:
Deep grey matter and brainstem nuclei have among the highest oxidative demands in the body, and in complex I deficiency they are where the lesions appear. Both 2018 patients showed progressive symmetrical basal ganglia change on neuroimaging, extending to the brain stem in one and to the internal capsule in the other - the Leigh-like pattern the paper's title names. The third reported patient instead had cavitating leukoencephalopathy, so the imaging phenotype of the entity is not confined to a single pattern.
Why these particular structures fail while others do not is the standing unanswered question of Leigh-syndrome biology generally, and nothing in the NDUFB8 literature addresses it; the node asserts the regional vulnerability, not an explanation for it.

nodes.description: NDUFB8 sits at the distal, proton-pumping end of complex I in the ND5 module, spanning the inner membrane once with its N-terminus in the matrix and its C-terminus in the intermembrane space. Its defining structural role is to clamp the long lateral helix of the core subunit ND5; on the matrix side it also contacts ND5 and NDUFB4 and, more weakly, ND4 and NDUFB9, and on the intermembrane-space side NDUFB7 and NDUFB10. With NDUFB3 and NDUFB6 it encloses the distal end of the enzyme. Losing it therefore removes a structural brace at a module interface rather than a catalytic component.

nodes.description: The c.432C>G (p.Cys144Trp) allele behaves mostly as a splicing variant rather than a missense one. It creates a new exonic splicing silencer, and Sanger sequencing of patient cDNA showed skipping of exon 4, which encodes Met105 to Val156 - the segment carrying the transmembrane helix. Skipping is favoured but not complete: about 14 percent of total cDNA still carried the missense sequence, so the allele produces a mixture of a large in-frame-disrupting deletion product and a low level of full-length mutant protein. This is the one place in the entity where the molecular consequence of an allele is not what its protein-level nomenclature suggests.

nodes.description:
Without NDUFB8 the enzyme does not assemble. In a human knockout cell line the loss of NDUFB8 leaves no assembled complex I detectable, and NDUFB8 falls among the 25 accessory subunits that a systematic gene-editing survey found to be strictly required for a functional complex. The general rule established by that survey - that losing one subunit destabilises the other subunits of its own structural module - is the mechanism by which a single missing brace propagates into a whole-enzyme failure.
The knockout evidence is a complete null; the patient alleles are not, which is why this node is written as a failure of assembly rather than an absence of the enzyme, and why patients retain measurable residual activity.
nodes.id: Failure of Complex I Holoenzyme Assembly

nodes.description:
Complex I is the entry point for NADH-derived electrons into the respiratory chain and pumps four protons per NADH oxidised, so a complex I defect cuts both the electron flux into the chain and the proton-motive force that drives ATP synthesis. Cells retain succinate-driven, complex II-dependent respiration, which is why the defect is survivable at all and why severity tracks residual complex I activity and tissue energy demand rather than being uniformly lethal.
This node is a mechanistic inference from the measured enzyme deficiency above rather than a separately measured quantity in these patients: no respirometry or ATP-synthesis measurement from an NDUFB8 patient is reported in the sources cited here, beyond the statement that complementation restored mitochondrial function.
